dedupe_keys.name: nfpa fatal firefighter injuries in the united states annual report since 1977

description: This annual report counts and describes on-duty firefighter deaths in the United States. It is produced by the research division of the National Fire Protection Association, which has collected information on every on-duty firefighter fatality since 1977. Deaths are included if due to traumatic injury or to heart attacks, strokes, aneurysms or other medical conditions; since 2022 medical deaths within 24 hours of duty are also counted. The latest report identifies 83 fatalities in 2025, up from 69 in 2024, of which 79 were municipal firefighters (45 volunteer and 34 career) and four wildland firefighters, with 65 meeting the historical on-duty criteria. Tables break deaths down by cause, type of duty, such as fireground, responding or training, age and department type, with long-run trends. Coverage is national and annual. The summary is free to read online and the full report is free to download as a PDF; NFPA retains copyright. Caveats: counts depend on NFPA's inclusion criteria, which changed in 2022, and are not directly comparable with the US Fire Administration's own fatality series. Simulation uses: responder casualty rates for emergency service workforce and resilience models. Related records: the US Fire Administration reports (data-usfa-fire-department-firefighter-reports) and the NIFC wildland fire statistics (data-nifc-wildland-fire-statistics) cover related series.
